title: Word Search in Grid
statement: Given a 2-D grid of single-character strings (a list of lists of length-1 strings) and a target word, determine whether the word can be formed by a path of adjacent cells. Adjacent means sharing an edge (up, down, left, or right); the same cell may not be used more than once within a single path. Return True if such a path exists, otherwise False.
hints: This is a backtracking search over grid paths: try starting the word at every cell and explore neighbors depth-first.

Track visited cells for the current path only (not globally) so a path can revisit a cell after backtracking away from a dead end, and prune as soon as a cell's letter doesn't match the expected character.

For each starting cell, run backtrack(r, c, i, visited): if grid[r][c] != word[i] return False; if i is the last index return True; else mark (r,c) visited, try the 4 neighbors recursing with i+1, unmark before returning. Return True if any start succeeds.
